1_connect.answer: connect accepts exactly one dial algorithm: to (single), serial (array), parallel (array) or serial_parallel (array of arrays; outer serial, inner parallel). Destinations can be E.164 numbers, sip: URIs, Resource Addresses like /public/name or /private/name, queue:name, or stream:wss://. Top-level props: from, from_name, headers (array of {name,value}, SIP only), codecs, webrtc_media, encryption, session_timeout, timeout (default 60), max_duration (schema default 14400), answer_on_bridge (default false), ringback, confirm, confirm_timeout, call_state_url, call_state_events (default [ended]), status_url, result, plus transfer_after_bridge in schema. Per-destination from/from_name/timeout/call_state_url/etc override top level. connect_result is connected or failed; return_value equals connect_result; connect_failed_reason is a free-form 'detailed reason' with no enumerated values. No maximum parallel destination count is documented (schema has no maxItems; a limit of 20 is not documented). call_state_url posts event_type calling.call.state; status_url posts event_type calling.call.connect.
exact_fields: call_state_url payload: event_type (calling.call.state), event_channel, timestamp, project_id, space_id, params.call_id, params.node_id, params.call_state (created|ringing|answered|ended), params.direction, params.device.type, params.device.params.from_number, params.device.params.to_number, params.end_reason (hangup|busy|no_answer|cancel|declined|error)

status_url payload: event_type (calling.call.connect), event_channel, timestamp, project_id, space_id, params.call_id, params.node_id, params.segment_id, params.tag, params.connect_state (connecting|connected|failed|disconnected), params.failed_reason, params.peer.call_id, params.peer.tag, params.peer.node_id, params.peer.queue_id, params.peer.queue_name, params.peer.device
quotes: connect_result:** (out) `connected` | `failed`.
connect_failed_reason:** (out) Detailed reason for failure.
return_value:** (out) Same value as `connect_result`.
`connect.headers` (object[]): Custom SIP headers to add to INVITE. Has no effect on calls to phone numbers.
`connect.answer_on_bridge` (boolean): Delay answer until the B-leg answers.
`connect.max_duration` (integer): Maximum duration, in seconds, allowed for the call.
`connect.from` (string): Caller ID number. Optional. Can be overwritten on each destination.
"max_duration": ... "default": 14400 ... "Maximum duration, in seconds, allowed for the call.\nDefault is `14400` seconds." (schema)
"timeout": ... "default": 60 ... "Time, in seconds, to wait for the call to be answered.\nDefault is 60 seconds." (schema)
"parallel": {"type": "array", "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/ConnectDeviceSingle"}, "description": "Array of destinations to dial simultaneously."} (schema, no maxItems)

`serial_parallel[][].to` (string, required): Destination to dial. Can be: - Phone number in E.164 format (e.g., `+15552345678`) - SIP URI (e.g., `sip:alice@example.com`) - Resource Address (e.g., `/public/test_room`) - Queue (e.g., `queue:support`) - WebSocket stream (e.g., `stream:wss://example.com/audio`)
A POST request will be sent to `call_state_url` with a JSON payload when the call state changes. Only events listed in `call_state_events` will be sent (default: `ended`).
`params.end_reason` (string): The reason the call ended (only present when `call_state` is `ended`). **Valid values:** `hangup`, `busy`, `no_answer`, `cancel`, `declined`, `error`.
`event_type` (string): The type of event. Always `calling.call.connect` for connect status events.
`params.failed_reason` (string): The reason the connection failed. Only present when `connect_state` is `failed`.
a Subscriber named `Bob` in the `private` context is reachable at `/private/bob`, or, from within that context, just `/bob`.
gaps: Maximum number of parallel destinations: not documented in sources searched (connect page chunks, SWML JSON schema grep for maxItems = 0 hits, internal reference, cheatsheet, queries 'connect parallel destinations limit maximum 10 20'). The figure 20 is not documented. (Only cXML <Dial> documents 'up to 10 <Sip>s within a <Dial>', which is a different product.)

connect_failed_reason enumerated values: not documented in sources searched; only 'Detailed reason for failure'. Related enumerations that are documented elsewhere: call_state_url params.end_reason (hangup|busy|no_answer|cancel|declined|error) and RELAY end reasons (hangup, cancel, busy, noAnswer, decline, error, abandoned, max_duration, not_found). Do not assume these equal connect_failed_reason.

status_url on connect: public page documents it, but the SWML JSON schema connect device defs do not list a top-level status_url property (only call_state_url); validators using the schema may reject it.
A 'fabric:' URI scheme for SWML connect.to is not documented; Resource Addresses are written as /context/name. ('fabric' appears only as a RELAY device type.)
Whether headers apply to Resource Address (WebRTC subscriber) destinations is not documented; docs say only 'Has no effect on calls to phone numbers'.

2_switch_cond_voicemail.answer: connect.result is a switch on return_value (=connect_result) when an object, or a cond when an array; ConnectSwitch.variable defaults to connect_result. Standalone switch takes variable, case, default. cond is an array of {when, then} plus optional {else}. Documented voicemail pattern: connect with result.case.connected [hangup], default [execute voicemail, hangup]. record (foreground, 'recording for voicemails') sets record_url and record_result; example plays it back with play %{record_url}.
quotes: "variable": {"type": "string", "examples": ["connect_result"], "description": "Name of the variable whose value needs to be compared. If not provided, it will check the `connect_result` variable."} (schema ConnectSwitch)
**result:** Optional `switch` on `return_value` when object `{}` or `cond` when array `[]`
##### JSON, Dial single phone number, go to voicemail on failure ... "result": { "case": { "connected": [ "hangup" ] }, "default": [ { "execute": "voicemail" }, "hangup" ] }
Record call audio in foreground. This is recording for voicemails.
- **record_url:** (out) the URL of the newly created recording
- **record_result:** (out) success | failed
gaps: Cheatsheet lists record output var record_duration; the reference and public pages searched list only record_url and record_result. Treat record_duration as unconfirmed.
A full end-to-end voicemail recipe (greeting wav + beep + record + store) was not found as a public doc page; the pattern is assembled from connect.result example and record example.

Cheatsheet record.direction comment says 'speak, hear, both'; internal reference says speak/hear (record default speak); public record_call page says speak/listen/both. Value spelling for record (not record_call) 'listen' vs 'hear' is inconsistent across sources.

3_record_call.answer: record_call (background) props: control_id, stereo (default false), format wav|mp3|mp4 (default wav), direction speak|listen|both (default both), terminators, beep (default false), input_sensitivity, initial_timeout, end_silence_timeout, max_length, status_url. Sets record_call_url, record_call_result (success|failed), record_control_id. stop_record_call takes control_id (optional; default stops last started) and sets stop_record_call_result. status_url posts event_type calling.call.record with params.state recording|paused|finished|no_input|error and url, recording_id, duration, size, start_time, end_time, first_frame_time, segment_id, record.audio.{format,direction,stereo}.
quotes: `record_call.format` (string): Format (`"wav"`, `"mp3"`, or `"mp4"`)
`record_call.direction` (string): Direction of the audio to record: `"speak"` for what party says, `"listen"` for what party hears, `"both"` for what the party hears and says
`params.state` (string): The current recording state. **Valid values:** `recording`, `paused`, `finished`, `no_input`, `error`.
The `finished` event has `params.url`, `params.duration`, and `params.size`. `params.recording_id` matches the `id` the Recordings API returns.
- **control_id:** String, Optional ID of the recording to stop. If not set, the last recording started will be stopped.
gaps: Which channel is which in a stereo recording (caller vs callee, left vs right) is not documented in sources searched.
Whether record_call started on the A-leg before connect keeps recording the bridged B-leg audio is not explicitly documented.

4_play_answer_hangup_transfer_execute.answer: play: url or urls; schemes http(s):// audio file, say:, silence:<seconds>, ring:<duration>:<country>; volume -40..40; loop (default 1, 0 = loop until call ends or play stopped); say_voice/say_language/say_gender; auto_answer; status_url (event calling.call.play, params.state playing|paused|finished|error). answer: max_duration (min 7, default 14400), codecs. hangup: reason hangup|busy|decline (internal reference says default busy). transfer: dest (URL, sends HTTP POST) + params; tail call, does not return. execute: dest (section label or URL), params, result (switch/cond on return_value), on_return; subroutine returns via return.
quotes: - **`loop:`** Number, Optional number of times to play the file(s). Default 1. 0 will loop until the call ends or the play is stopped.
- **`silence:<duration>`** - seconds of silence to play
- **max_duration:** Optional maximum duration in seconds. Can not be less than 7 seconds. Default is 14400 seconds (4 hours).
- **reason:** Optional hangup reason (hangup, busy, decline). Default is busy.
- **`https://<URL>`** - URL to fetch next document from. Sends HTTP POST
Execute a section or URL as a subroutine and return back to current document.
gaps: hangup default reason 'busy' comes from the internal reference only; public hangup page was not retrieved. Verify before relying on it.
Supported wav encodings/sample rates for play URLs: not documented in sources searched.

5_external_swml_webhook_request.answer: SignalWire sends HTTP POST with a JSON body to the External URL (Primary Script URL / primary_request_url), and on failure to fallback_request_url with the same payload. Body top-level keys: call, vars, envs, params (params empty {} on the initial inbound fetch; vars not in the initial inbound payload). call fields: call_id, call_state, direction (inbound|outbound), from, to, headers[] {name,value}, node_id, project_id, segment_id, space_id, type (sip|phone|webrtc), sip_data (sip only). Response must be application/json, application/yaml or text/x-yaml. primary_request_method / fallback_request_method exist (fallback GET or POST).
quotes: `call.from` (string): The number/URI that initiated this call.
`call.type` (string): The type of call. Possible values: `sip`, `phone`, `webrtc`.
`params` (object): Parameters passed by the calling `execute` or `transfer` step. Empty `{}` on the initial inbound fetch.
`vars` (object): Runtime variable scope, populated by methods as the script executes. **Not part of the initial inbound payload**

The `raw_body` is the JSON payload exactly as sent ... the object containing `call` (or `message` for a messaging document), `vars`, `envs`, and, when the document was reached through `execute` or `transfer`, `params`.
Your server must respond with a valid SWML document using one of these content types: `application/json`, `application/yaml`, or `text/x-yaml`.
`fallback_request_url` (string): Fallback URL SignalWire fetches the SWML document from if the primary URL fails. Receives the same payload as `primary_request_url`
gaps: Which field identifies the calling Subscriber when a browser Subscriber dials an address: not documented in sources searched. Docs only say call.from is 'The number/URI that initiated this call' and call.type can be 'webrtc'; no example shows call.from for a subscriber (e.g. whether it is /private/name, an email, a subscriber id, or a fabric URI). Must be captured empirically.
call.from_number, call.caller_id_name, call.caller_id_number: not documented for SWML fetch payload (from_number appears only inside call_state_url params.device.params).
vars.userVariables: appears only in SDK SWAIG function payload examples (signalwire-python cli_guide), not in the SWML document-fetch payload docs. Not documented for SWML fetch.
An 'envelope' wrapper field: not documented in sources searched.
Shape of envs object (keys) not documented in chunks retrieved.

Full verbatim example payload from the public inbound-call-webhook reference (/docs/apis/rest/webhooks/inbound-call-webhook) was not retrievable; only an older internal example (mcp get_swml reference) with call.state, call.type=sip, from/to as sip: URIs.

6_webhook_signature.answer: Key = project Signing Key from Dashboard API Credentials (per project), not the API token. For SWML document fetches (JSON): X-Signalwire-Signature = hex(HMAC-SHA1(signing_key, url + raw_body)) sent on every signed request; X-Signalwire-SHA256-Signature = hex(HMAC-SHA256(signing_key, url + raw_body)) sent on call requests. url is the full requested URL incl. query string; for call requests embedded basic-auth credentials are stripped before signing. No separator; raw body bytes. Compatibility/cXML form posts: base64 HMAC-SHA1 over URL + sorted form param name+value pairs (validator tries with and without default port; bodySHA256 query param for JSON posts). X-Twilio-Signature accepted by SDK validators in place of X-SignalWire-Signature. Helpers: @signalwire/compatibility-api RestClient.validateRequest(signingKey, signature, url, body); @signalwire/js validateRequest(...) with raw body; Python signalwire.core.security validate_webhook_signature(signing_key, signature, url, raw_body), validate_webhook_signature_sha256, legacy validate_request(signing_key, signature, url, params_or_raw_body); TypeScript @signalwire/sdk webhookValidationMiddleware, validateWebhookSignature, validateWebhookSignatureSha256, validateRequest.
quotes: | `X-Signalwire-Signature` | HMAC-SHA1, hex encoded | Every signed request |
| `X-Signalwire-SHA256-Signature` | HMAC-SHA256, hex encoded | Call requests |
Both are computed over the same string: the request URL concatenated directly with the raw request body, with no separator.
signature = hex( HMAC( signing_key, url + raw_body ) )
A call request signs that URL without any basic auth credentials you embedded in it; a message request signs it exactly as you configured it, credentials included.

**Scheme B: form-encoded requests** (cXML and other compatibility endpoints). The form parameters are sorted by name, and each name and value is appended to the URL; a repeated name keeps its values in their original order. The signature is the standard base64 HMAC-SHA1 of that string.
The key was just rotated.** A new key needs about a minute to become active.
gaps: Header name casing differs across docs: X-Signalwire-Signature / X-Signalwire-SHA256-Signature (SWML guide) vs X-SignalWire-Signature / X-SignalWire-Sha256-Signature (SDK docs). HTTP headers are case-insensitive; read them case-insensitively.

Whether call_state_url / status_url / record_call status callbacks carry the SHA256 header (vs SHA1 only) is not stated explicitly for SWML status callbacks; Python SDK docs say every outbound webhook incl. RELAY async events is signed.
Signature behavior when the Resource URL includes a URL fragment (#ot=...) not documented.

7_webhook_reliability.answer: SWML External URL resources have a primary URL and an optional fallback URL (fallback_request_url / fallback_request_method GET|POST). Server SDK guide: fallback triggers on connection timeout, HTTP 5xx, invalid SWML response; SignalWire waits about 5 seconds for SWML. Failure surfaces as SWML error http_retrieval_error. Retry counts for SWML document fetch are not documented. Compatibility API (cXML) documents 2 s connect / 5 s read timeouts, URL fragment overrides ot/rt/tt, action webhooks not retried but go to fallback, status callbacks retried up to 2 more times (3 total); these are cXML-specific.
quotes: **Fallback triggers on:** - Connection timeout - HTTP 5xx errors - Invalid SWML response
SignalWire waits ~5 seconds for SWML
`http_retrieval_error` (string): The attempt to retrieve the SWML document timed out or failed.
Our current timeouts are 2 seconds for Connect and 5 seconds for Read. (Compatibility API)
If it's a status callback webhook, SignalWire will retry up to two more times (Compatibility API; original text uses an em-dash before 'three attempts in total')
gaps: Retry policy (count/backoff) for SWML document fetch on 5xx or timeout: not documented in sources searched; only fallback behavior.
Retry policy for SWML status callbacks (call_state_url, connect status_url, record_call status_url): not documented for SWML; only cXML status callback retries are documented.
Exact SWML fetch timeout is '~5 seconds' (approximate, Server SDK troubleshooting page); no authoritative connect/read split for SWML.
Whether 4xx responses trigger fallback: not documented.
Whether cXML URL-fragment timeout overrides (#ot=, #rt=, #tt=) apply to SWML URLs: not documented.

8_caller_id_to_subscriber.answer: connect.from sets the caller ID number on the outbound leg ('Default is calling party caller ID number' per internal reference), overridable per destination; from_name applies to SIP only. The forwarding guide shows from: %{call.from} to preserve original caller. What a browser Subscriber's SDK displays as the caller for an inbound call, and whether connect.from overrides it for a Resource Address (/private/name) destination, is not documented.
quotes: - **from:** String, Optional. Caller ID number. Default is calling party caller ID number. Can be overwritten on each destination. (internal reference)
`connect.from_name` (string): The caller ID name shown to the person you're calling, displayed alongside the `from` number (sometimes called CNAM). Applies to SIP calls only
Notice how we used its `from` parameter to ensure that the number of the original caller (stored in the `call.from` variable) is maintained as caller ID for the forwarded call.
gaps: Caller ID presented to a Subscriber/browser on inbound calls: not documented in sources searched (queries: 'incoming call to subscriber caller id displayed browser SDK', 'Browser SDK v4 incoming call ... Call.from').
Whether connect.from overrides caller ID for Resource Address / WebRTC destinations: not documented; from_name explicitly SIP-only.

9_hold.answer: RELAY server-side call.hold(): 'The remote party hears hold music or silence while the call is held.' Browser SDK exposes call.toggleHold() in examples, but no Browser SDK / Call Fabric doc retrieved states what the remote party hears.
quotes: Put the call on hold. The remote party hears hold music or silence while the call is held.
async function toggleHold(call) { await call.toggleHold(); }
gaps: What the remote party hears when a Browser SDK (Call Fabric) Subscriber puts a call on hold: not documented in sources searched (query 'browser SDK hold call remote party hears music on hold'). RELAY text says 'hold music or silence' without specifying which or how to configure.
Configurable music-on-hold for Call Fabric / Browser SDK hold: not documented.
